subject: Recap + next steps: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Iqbal <sasha@brightbridge.ai>, Dev Ops Team <infra@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the candid rundown of where BrightBridge is with models and where you need to go. Short recap and proposed next steps below.

Highlights / pain points you called out:
- Heavy reliance on OpenAI + Anthropic for both chat and embeddings; token costs are rising and latency spikes during peak inference windows.
- Tooling lock-in: function/tool calling and structured output pipelines are tuned to the existing APIs, so compatibility is a key risk for cutover.
- Compliance needs: data residency (EU customers) and KMS/HSM integration for encryption-at-rest and auditability.
- Throughput & concurrency: customer-facing chat peaks require predictable throughput; current autoscaling causes variable latency.

Current stack (as described):
- Frontend: React + server-side aggregator
- API: Requests hit an internal broker that fans out to OpenAI/Anthropic with a shared caching layer (Redis) for short-term prefixes and embeddings in Postgres
- Auth: SSO via Okta; keys are centrally managed today in vendor consoles

Success criteria you want from an offramp:
1) Latency parity within 20% of current p95 for common prompts
2) Embedding/semantic search compatibility so relevance doesn't regress >5% on your evaluation set
3) Cost reduction target: 30% lower per-1M tokens and embedding unit economics within 45 days
4) Ability to retain existing tool-calling hooks or map them with minimal app change
5) KMS integration + EU data residency option

Initial model shortlist / fit candidates (rough, to align expectations):
- Llama 2 variants (13B q4f/70B quantized) — strong candidate for chat parity with quantized performance profiles
- Mistral Instruct (7B/12B) — good balance for instruction following and lower cost at mid-sized sequences
- Vicuna / fine-tuned LLM variants for rapid adaptation of your assistant persona
- Open-source embedding models (e.g., Ada-like replacements) for compatibility testing with your vector stack

Proposed next steps (we agreed on these):
- We will send a short Mutual Action Plan (attached) and an offramp playbook that outlines data handling, POC template, and test harnesses. (Attached: redwood-offramp-playbook.pdf, mutual-action-plan-template.xlsx)
- BrightBridge to share a small evaluation dataset (5–10 representative prompts + embedding sample) and the current p95/p50 latency numbers by EOW (Aug 21).
- Redwood to provision a two-week POC environment (sandbox / VPC option) using a recommended model (we suggested Llama-2-13B q4f as a starting point) and a test harness to measure latency, quality, and cost.
- Security: we'll run through the security questionnaire and flag KMS/residency items — Karthik will own the questionnaire follow-up.

Timing: target POC start: Aug 25. Post-POC readout and scorecard: Sept 8.

If that all matches your read, Sasha, reply here and we'll lock the MAP and POC schedule.

Thanks,
Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0124

Attachment stubs: redwood-offramp-playbook.pdf (28 pages, PDF), mutual-action-plan-template.xlsx (Excel, blank MAP template)

From: Sasha Iqbal <sasha@brightbridge.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Ops Team <infra@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks Jonas — that summary looks right to me. A few clarifications:
- Evaluation dataset: we'll redline anything proprietary, but can share a sanitized set and the embedding index snapshot by Aug 21.
- KMS / residency: EU customers are the blocker for an initial pilot; we need to see how your private deployment handles key custody and an EU region.
- Tool calling: biggest risk is webhook payload shapes — if you can provide a compatibility shim or mapping guide during POC that would be huge.

We're happy to proceed with the Aug 25 POC start. I can bring our infra lead (Marta) into the kickoff if that helps.

One more ask: can you confirm which metrics you'll measure in the POC readout so we can align instrumentation?

— Sasha
Director of Product, BrightBridge AI
Sasha@brightbridge.ai

On the attachments: we'll take the MAP and attachments and comment — thanks for sending them early.

- We'll default to Llama-2-13B q4f for the POC unless Karthik suggests otherwise after the security review.

I'll schedule the Aug 25 kickoff (30 min) once Sasha confirms Marta's availability.

Jonas

Thanks Sasha — great. Short answers to your items and next steps: 

POC metrics we'll capture (we'll include these in the MAP):
- Latency: p50/p95 token generation latency for a suite of canonical prompts (match against your provided baseline)
- Quality: embedding similarity stability (recall@10) and a small human-blind A/B on 300 prompts to measure semantic parity
- Cost: per-token and per-embedding projected cost for steady-state and peak scenarios
- Compatibility: success rate for existing function/tool call mappings; number of payload transformations required

Security & residency: Karthik will run the KMS/HSM checklist and confirm EU region options by Aug 21.

Kickoff: Aug 25 09:00 PT (30m) — I've tentatively scheduled and sent a calendar invite. Marta welcome; feel free to add any infra folks who should be in the POC channel.

Next artifact: I'll drop a short POC runbook (test harness commands and postman collection) before Friday. In the meantime, please upload the sanitized prompt set and an example embedding snapshot to the Drive link in the MAP.

Looking forward — see you on the 25th.

Jonas
